md_description: This DAG describes an ex vivo rodent brain-slice electrophysiology workflow used to study how pharmacological modulation of neurotransmitter receptors affects synaptic plasticity. It includes tissue preparation, patch-clamp acquisition of synaptic responses, processing of raw recordings into quantitative response metrics, and generation of a metadata-rich analysis table linking species, brain region, neurotransmitter systems, causal interactions, and supporting publications.

rodent_brain.reasoning: The rodent_brain node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic specimen-origin and biological identity fields relevant to the intact source tissue. I excluded any preparation, incubation, pharmacology, recording, processing, or analysis details because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided generic experiment identifiers because those are typically generated once at the root and may overlap with already_generated fields; since none were provided here, I limited the schema to core tissue provenance and biological descriptors needed to understand the source of the slices.

md_schema.descr: Rodent species of the intact source brain tissue used to prepare acute slices; record the organism at specimen origin, before any dissection or slicing. Examples: Mus musculus, Rattus norvegicus.
Inbred or outbred rodent strain of the source brain tissue, recorded at specimen origin to support biological reproducibility. Examples: C57BL/6J, Sprague Dawley, Wistar.
Biological sex of the rodent from which the intact brain was obtained; record at tissue origin, not inferred from downstream samples. Examples: male, female, unknown.
Age of the rodent at the time the intact brain was collected, reported in the study's native unit to contextualize developmental stage. Typical examples: postnatal day 21, 8 weeks, 3 months.
Anatomical brain region of the intact tissue source that was dissected for slice preparation. Record the region as specified in the experiment. Examples: hippocampus, cortex, striatum, thalamus.
Developmental stage of the rodent source tissue, if explicitly reported, used to contextualize the intrinsic state of the intact brain prior to slicing. Examples: juvenile, adolescent, adult.
Local identifier for the intact rodent brain specimen used as input to slice preparation; use a stable string format such as animal ID or cohort code (for example, animal_07 or rat_A12).

Genetic background or engineered genotype of the rodent source tissue, recorded as an intrinsic property of the animal before any experimental manipulation. Examples: wild type, receptor knockout, transgenic line name.

acute_brain_slice.reasoning: The acute_brain_slice node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared slice itself: where it came from, how it was cut, its physical dimensions, orientation, viability, and the slice's biological composition/state immediately after preparation. I excluded preparation protocol details, incubation conditions, recording setup, drug treatment, raw signal properties, and computed outputs because those belong to the upstream slice_preparation/slice_recovery processes or downstream capture/signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any specimen-origin fields that would belong to rodent_brain if already generated there; this schema focuses on the slice as the distinct object created from that source.

md_schema.descr: Brain region from which the acute slice was prepared, recorded at the slice entity level to preserve provenance of the dissected tissue. Example: hippocampus, prefrontal cortex.
Thickness of the acute brain slice measured after cutting and before recording, in micrometers; typically recorded to indicate physical preparation quality. Typical range: 200-500 micrometer.
Orientation of the cut relative to the source brain anatomy, recorded for the prepared slice because it affects preserved circuits. Examples: coronal, sagittal, horizontal, oblique.
Qualitative viability assessment of the prepared acute slice at the time it is selected for downstream recovery or recording. Examples: viable, partially viable, nonviable, not assessed.
Biological state of the slice as a living ex vivo preparation ready for electrophysiology; use this to distinguish the entity from fixed or dead tissue. Example values: living_ex_vivo, fixed, frozen.
Local identifier for the individual acute slice, using a stable string format such as slice_01 or animal_07_slice_b.
Number of acute slices prepared from the source brain for this specimen or preparation batch; record at the slice entity/batch level after cutting. Typical range: 1-20.
Approximate anterior-posterior level or atlas level of the slice, recorded to support circuit-level interpretation. Examples: bregma -1.8 mm, dorsal hippocampus level, cortical level.

slice_in_acsf.reasoning: I removed the colliding field slice_identifier because already_generated indicates it was produced for an earlier DAG step, and entity identifiers must not be repeated across nodes. The remaining fields stay within the slice_in_acsf entity territory by describing the maintained slice's state in ACSF, its solution context, temperature, oxygenation, equilibration, and readiness for recording. I excluded any capture, signal, process, or root-specimen fields to avoid crossing semantic boundaries.

md_schema.descr: Name of the physiological recording/holding solution the slice is maintained in prior to electrophysiological measurement. For this workflow, record the ACSF formulation name or lab-specific equivalent as stated in the protocol.

Qualitative state of the slice while it is maintained in solution immediately before recording. This describes the entity state, not the protocol. Example values: equilibrated, oxygenated, temperature_controlled, ready_for_recording.

Temperature of the slice while it is held in ACSF immediately before electrophysiological measurement, in degrees Celsius. Typical range for ex vivo slice maintenance: 0-37 celsius depending on protocol; record the actual holding temperature used here.
Duration that the slice has been maintained in ACSF prior to recording, measured from transfer into the solution to the start of capture. Typical range: 5-240 minutes.

Whether the ACSF holding solution is actively oxygenated while the slice is maintained for recording. Record the state at the slice entity level immediately before capture. Examples: carbogenated, oxygenated, not_oxygenated, unknown.
Boolean flag indicating whether the slice is judged suitable and ready for downstream patch-clamp measurement after maintenance in ACSF.

Brief description or label of the ACSF composition used to maintain the slice, as an entity attribute of the maintained slice. Examples: standard ACSF, sucrose-based ACSF, modified ACSF with elevated Mg2+.

slice_preparation.reasoning: The slice_preparation node is a Process, so I included only parameters of the dissection and slicing operation itself: how the tissue was cut, with what instrument/approach, under what protective conditions, and the immediate quality outcome of the cut. I excluded specimen identity fields because those belong to the upstream rodent_brain entity, and I excluded downstream slice properties such as thickness or orientation when they are better represented on the acute_brain_slice entity. I also avoided the previously generated slice_identifier field per the collision notice, and I kept the schema focused on reproducible preparation settings that a downstream user would need to repeat the slicing step.

md_schema.descr: Medium used during brain dissection and slicing to protect tissue viability at the moment the rodent brain is removed and cut. Examples: ice-cold sucrose ACSF, ice-cold oxygenated ACSF, protective cutting solution.
Temperature of the tissue and cutting medium during the slicing operation, measured at the time the brain is cut into acute slices. Typical range: 0-10 celsius for cold slicing protocols.
Instrument used to cut the rodent brain into acute slices during the preparation process. Examples: vibratome, tissue chopper, microslicer.
Qualitative description of how the brain was cut into slices during preparation. Examples: coronal sectioning, sagittal sectioning, horizontal sectioning.
Target thickness set during the slicing process, in micrometers; record the intended cut thickness specified by the operator or protocol at the time of preparation. Typical range: 200-500 micrometer.

Operator-selected speed or advancement setting used on the slicing instrument during preparation, recorded as the instrument's native setting or a normalized label. Include this because it affects slice quality and reproducibility.
Immediate qualitative assessment of the slicing outcome after cutting, such as whether the acute slices were suitable for recovery and recording. Examples: acceptable, damaged, poor, excellent.
Total duration of the dissection and cutting step from removal of the brain to completion of slice production, in minutes. Typical range: 5-60 minutes.

slice_recovery.reasoning: The slice_recovery node is a Process, so I included only incubation and stabilization parameters that define how recovery was performed: solution identity, oxygenation, temperature, duration, and a simple quality outcome for the recovery step. I excluded slice identity, cutting details, and downstream recording/capture information because those belong to the acute_brain_slice entity, slice_preparation process, or patch_clamp_recording capture. I also avoided duplicating any maintained-slice state fields already used on slice_in_acsf, keeping this schema focused on the operational recovery step itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the oxygenated recording solution used during the slice recovery incubation step. For this workflow, record the ACSF formulation or lab-specific equivalent used to stabilize the tissue before recording.
Temperature at which the acute slice is incubated during recovery, measured at the time the recovery process is performed. Typical range for ex vivo recovery: 20-37 celsius depending on protocol.
Duration of the recovery incubation in oxygenated solution, measured from the start of incubation until the slice is transferred to the recording-ready state. Typical range: 10-180 minutes.
Gas mixture used to oxygenate the recovery solution during incubation. Record the operator-controlled oxygenation condition at the process level. Examples: carbogen, 95% O2/5% CO2, 100% O2.
How the slice was held during recovery incubation. Examples: submerged, interface, continuously perfused, static bath.

Immediate qualitative assessment of how well the slice stabilized after recovery incubation, recorded at the end of the process before downstream modulation or recording. Examples: good, moderate, poor, not_assessed.

pharmacological_modulation.reasoning: The pharmacological_modulation node is a Process, so I included only the intervention parameters used to apply drugs to the slice: target receptor/system, agent identity, dose, timing, route, and the intended modulation type. I excluded any downstream treatment-state identifiers, recording file properties, or response metrics because those belong to the treated_slice entity or later capture/signal/derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating general specimen or slice provenance fields already handled upstream, and I kept the schema centered on reproducible drug application details needed to interpret the causal manipulation.

md_schema.descr: Primary neurotransmitter receptor targeted by the pharmacological agent applied during modulation, recorded at the process step where the drug is introduced to the slice. Examples: NMDA receptor, AMPA receptor, GABA_A receptor, mGluR5.
Neurotransmitter system being modulated by the applied pharmacological agent at this step. Examples: glutamatergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, dopaminergic, serotonergic.
Name of the agonist or antagonist applied to the slice during the modulation process. Use the compound's common name or laboratory label. Example: AP5, CNQX, bicuculline, TTX.
Pharmacological class of the applied compound, recorded at the time of modulation. Examples: agonist, antagonist, positive_allosteric_modulator, negative_allosteric_modulator, uptake_inhibitor.
Final concentration of the pharmacological agent in the bath during application, in micromolar; measure or calculate at the point of exposure in the slice bath. Typical range: 0.001-1000 micromolar.
Duration of exposure to the pharmacological agent, measured from the start of drug application to the end of the defined modulation window. Typical range: 1-240 minutes.
How the pharmacological agent was delivered to the slice during modulation. Examples: bath_application, local_puff, pressure_ejection, perfusion.
Whether the applied pharmacological agent was washed out after the modulation period, recorded at the end of the process. This helps interpret reversible versus persistent effects.

Whether the pharmacological intervention was intended to enhance or suppress receptor-mediated signaling in the slice. Record the intended direction of effect from the protocol. Examples: enhance, suppress, block, activate, unknown.

treated_slice.reasoning: The treated_slice node is an Entity, so I included only post-modulation state descriptors of the slice itself: which drug exposure it reflects, the treatment status, whether the effect was reversible, and whether the slice remains usable for downstream recording. I excluded the drug application protocol details because those belong to the pharmacological_modulation process, and I excluded recording/capture properties and signal quality metrics because those belong downstream. I also avoided repeating any slice identity fields already generated elsewhere and focused on the minimal entity attributes needed to distinguish the treated state from baseline or control slices.

md_schema.descr: State of the slice after receptor-targeting drug exposure, recorded as an entity attribute used to distinguish baseline, control, and treated material before recording. Examples: untreated, vehicle_control, treated.

Brief human-readable summary of the pharmacological exposure associated with this treated slice, including the agent name or target when relevant. Example: AP5-treated slice, bicuculline exposure, vehicle control.
Qualitative assessment of slice viability after drug exposure and before downstream patch-clamp recording. Examples: viable, partially_viable, nonviable, not_assessed.

Whether the observed treatment state is expected to be reversible after washout or persists as a stable treated condition. Record this at the treated slice entity level for interpretation of comparison recordings.
Label indicating which baseline or control group this treated slice is compared against in the experiment. Example values: baseline, vehicle_control, untreated_control, receptor_blocked.
Qualitative description of the slice's condition after drug exposure, immediately prior to downstream recording. Examples: stabilized, sensitized, suppressed, altered.

patch_clamp_recording.reasoning: The patch_clamp_recording node is a Capture, so I included only instrument configuration and acquisition-session parameters: amplifier/headstage identity, recording mode, electrode and bath settings, sampling and filtering, holding potential, and basic acquisition quality. I excluded slice properties, drug treatment details, raw file characteristics, and computed response metrics because those belong to the upstream treated_slice entity or downstream Signal/Derivative nodes. I also avoided generating fields that would duplicate software details if they are already represented on a Process node elsewhere in the DAG, and kept the schema focused on reproducible measurement-session setup and instrument configuration.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the patch-clamp amplifier used for the recording session; record the hardware brand that configured and acquired the electrophysiology measurement. Example: Molecular Devices, HEKA, Axon Instruments.
Model name or number of the patch-clamp amplifier used during acquisition. Example: MultiClamp 700B, EPC 10, Axopatch 200B.
Serial number of the patch-clamp amplifier or primary acquisition unit used for the recording session, recorded as a string identifier such as SN12345.
Model of the headstage connected to the recording amplifier during whole-cell patch-clamp acquisition. Record the hardware configuration used at the time of measurement.
Electrophysiological recording mode used during acquisition from the slice. Examples: whole_cell_voltage_clamp, whole_cell_current_clamp, cell_attached.
Digitization sampling rate applied during patch-clamp acquisition, measured at the instrument during the recording session. Typical range: 1000-50000 hz or higher depending on system.
Analog or hardware low-pass filter cutoff set on the amplifier during acquisition, in kilohertz. Typical range: 0.1-20 khz.
Membrane potential held by the amplifier during the recording session, in millivolts, recorded at the time of capture. Typical range: -120 to 60 mv depending on recording mode.
Patch pipette resistance measured before seal formation or at the start of the recording session, in megaohms. Typical range: 2-10 mohms for many whole-cell recordings.
Series/access resistance measured during the recording session, in megaohms, used as a session-level indicator of recording quality. Record at the time the cell is under whole-cell access.
Cell input resistance measured during the recording session, in megaohms, as part of the capture configuration/health assessment. Typical range depends on cell type.
Bath or chamber temperature actively controlled during electrophysiological acquisition, in degrees Celsius, measured during the capture session. Typical range: 20-37 celsius.
Qualitative seal status attained during the patch-clamp session. Examples: gigaseal, loose_seal, no_seal, whole_cell_established.
Immediate assessment of acquisition quality for the patch-clamp session, recorded during or right after capture. Examples: excellent, acceptable, noisy, unstable, failed.

raw_ephys_traces.reasoning: The raw_ephys_traces node is a Signal, so I included only properties of the raw data artefact itself: file format, size, dimensions, channel count, sampling characteristics as stored in the file, file location, and simple technical quality indicators. I excluded instrument settings, slice/treatment provenance, and any processed response metrics because those belong to the Capture, Entity, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided fields that would duplicate capture-session configuration or downstream analysis outputs, keeping the schema limited to what a downstream user needs to locate, inspect, and reuse the raw recordings.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw electrophysiology data file as stored by the acquisition or export system, for example a .abf, .dat, .tdms, or .csv file name.
Storage path or URI for the raw patch-clamp trace file, recorded at the signal artifact level to enable retrieval. Example: /data/session_01/raw/traces.abf or s3://bucket/run1/file.abf.
Digital file format of the unprocessed electrophysiology recording. Examples: ABF, TDMS, DAT, CSV, HDF5.
Size of the raw trace file in bytes, measured after acquisition/export and before any processing. Typical range depends on recording duration and channel count.
Number of individual trace sweeps, epochs, or continuous segments stored in the raw data file, as represented in the recorded signal artefact.
Number of acquisition channels present in the raw electrophysiology file, measured as the stored data dimensionality. Typical range: 1-64 depending on system.
Shape of the raw data array as stored in the file, recorded as a descriptive string such as samples_x_channels or sweeps_x_samples_x_channels.
Total duration of the unprocessed recording represented in the file, in seconds. Typical range depends on protocol and can span milliseconds to hours.
Sampling rate encoded in the raw data file metadata, in hertz, as stored after acquisition. This should match the file's technical representation rather than the amplifier setting if they differ.
Whether the raw signal file is compressed or uncompressed at rest. Examples: none, gzip, proprietary_compression.
Simple technical quality flag for the raw file itself, such as whether the trace is intact and readable before processing. Examples: valid, corrupted, truncated, partial, unknown.

trace_processing.reasoning: The trace_processing node is a Process, so I included only the analysis operations applied to the raw traces: software/pipeline identity, filtering and segmentation settings, baseline handling, event detection parameters, and the immediate processing outcome. I excluded raw file properties because those belong to raw_ephys_traces, and I excluded computed feature values themselves because those belong to the synaptic_response_metrics derivative. I also avoided repeating software metadata if already generated elsewhere, but because no collision list was provided for these exact names, I kept this schema focused on reproducible processing configuration and quality indicators for the transformation step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or pipeline used to process raw electrophysiology traces into quantitative features, recorded at the process step. Example: custom_python_pipeline, Clampfit, Neo, Spike2.
Version of the analysis software or pipeline used for trace processing, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: 1.2.0, 2024.03, v5.7.
Repository or source location for the processing code used on the raw traces, such as a Git URL, package name, or internal codebase identifier.
Type of digital filter applied during processing of the raw electrophysiology traces. Examples: low_pass, high_pass, band_pass, notch, none.

Cutoff frequency or frequencies used for digital filtering during processing, in hertz. For band-pass filters, record the effective band limits in the lab's standard string format if needed. Typical range: 0.1-5000 hz.
Time window used to segment traces into analysis epochs around stimulation or events, in milliseconds, measured during processing. Typical range: 1-10000 ms.
Method used to estimate and remove baseline from raw traces during processing. Examples: pre_event_mean, polynomial_fit, none.
Method used to detect synaptic events or response peaks in processed traces. Examples: threshold_crossing, template_matching, peak_finding, manual_annotation.

Rule or criteria used to exclude noisy or artifactual trace segments during processing, described as a string or rule label. Example: exclude sweeps with motion artifacts or access resistance > 20 MOhm.
Number of traces, sweeps, or segments retained after processing and quality filtering, recorded at the end of the trace_processing step.
Overall assessment of the processing outcome for the trace set. Examples: successful, partial, failed, review_required.

synaptic_response_metrics.reasoning: The synaptic_response_metrics node is a Derivative, so I included only computed outputs and their scientific summary characteristics: the metrics calculated from processed traces, the aggregation level, units, comparison basis, and confidence/quality indicators of the derived results. I excluded raw trace file properties, capture settings, and processing parameters because those belong upstream on the Signal, Capture, or Process nodes. I also avoided repeating fields already generated for causal interaction analysis or the final summary table, keeping this schema focused on the quantitative electrophysiology outputs themselves.

md_schema.descr: Name of the derived metric set computed from processed electrophysiology traces. Examples: synaptic amplitude_frequency_panel, plasticity_index_summary, evoked_response_metrics.
Type of quantitative response feature derived from the processed traces. Examples: amplitude, frequency, latency, rise_time, decay_time, plasticity_index.

Computed value of the response metric derived from the processed trace data, recorded in the units appropriate to the metric type at the time of derivation. Use a numeric value for a single primary metric when applicable.
Unit associated with the derived metric value. Examples: pA, mV, Hz, ms, unitless, percent.
Level at which the derived metric was summarized from the processed traces. Examples: sweep, cell, slice, condition, experiment.
Baseline or reference condition used when computing the metric or plasticity index. Examples: pre_treatment_baseline, vehicle_control, time_zero, untreated_control.
Direction of the computed plasticity effect when the metric represents change relative to baseline. Examples: potentiation, depression, no_change, mixed.
Number of traces, sweeps, cells, or slices contributing to the derived metric value, recorded at the derivation step. Typical range depends on analysis design.
Statistical uncertainty associated with the derived metric value, such as standard deviation, standard error, or confidence interval width, recorded in the same units or as a unitless summary.
Quality flag for the derived metric after computation. Examples: valid, noisy, outlier_suspect, insufficient_data, unknown.

causal_interaction_analysis.reasoning: The causal_interaction_analysis node is a Process, so I included only the inferential analysis parameters and outputs of the comparison step: the statistical framework, comparison groups, effect-size summary, significance criteria, multiple-testing handling, and a high-level confidence/strength assessment. I excluded raw metric definitions, capture settings, and the final curated table contents because those belong to upstream derivative nodes or to the downstream causal_plasticity_summary derivative. I also avoided repeating software metadata already assigned to earlier process nodes unless it is specific to this inference step, and I kept the schema centered on what is needed to reproduce and interpret the causal comparison between receptor manipulations and plasticity outcomes.

md_schema.descr: Name of the statistical or inference software/pipeline used to compare synaptic response metrics across receptor manipulations. Examples: custom_python_stats_pipeline, R, statsmodels, SciPy.
Version of the inference software or pipeline used for causal interaction analysis, recorded to support reproducibility. Example: 1.0.3, R 4.3.2.

Statistical or causal inference method used to compare response metrics across pharmacological conditions. Examples: t_test, anova, mixed_effects_model, permutation_test, bayesian_model, mediation_analysis.
Condition contrast evaluated in the causal analysis, such as treated versus baseline or receptor blocker versus vehicle. Record the exact groups compared at the inference step.

Summary statistic used to quantify the magnitude of the causal interaction between receptor manipulation and plasticity. Examples: mean_difference, log2_fold_change, Cohen_d, odds_ratio, beta_coefficient.
Numeric value of the estimated causal effect or interaction size derived from the comparison of synaptic response metrics across conditions. Use the primary effect estimate reported by the analysis.
P value or equivalent significance measure for the causal comparison between receptor manipulations, recorded at the analysis step. Typical range: 0-1.
Method used to correct for multiple comparisons in the causal analysis, if applicable. Examples: bonferroni, fdr_bh, none.
Decision threshold used to declare a causal interaction statistically significant, such as alpha level or posterior probability cutoff. Typical examples: 0.05, 0.01, 0.95.
Qualitative assessment of the strength of the inferred causal interaction between neurotransmitter receptor manipulation and synaptic plasticity. Examples: strong, moderate, weak, inconclusive.
Short textual summary of the inference result for the causal interaction analysis step, such as receptor blockade reduced plasticity or activation increased synaptic response.

causal_plasticity_summary.reasoning: I corrected the derivative-table schema by removing field names that collided with already generated metadata from earlier DAG steps: neurotransmitter_system, species, and brain_region. Because this node still represents the final compiled summary table, I retained only fields that are unique to the derived table itself: row identity, receptor-specific causal claim, effect direction, references, evidence support, confidence, and versioning. I also kept the schema within the derivative territory and avoided reintroducing raw or process-level details.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for each row in the derived causal plasticity summary table, used to track a single summarized interaction or evidence entry. Example format: cps_001 or row_12.
Specific receptor subtype or receptor family associated with the summarized causal interaction in the derived table. Examples: NMDA receptor, AMPA receptor, GABA_A receptor, mGluR5, D1 receptor.
Direction of the summarized causal effect on synaptic plasticity in the derived table. Examples: increased, decreased, bidirectional, no_effect, inconclusive.
Concise textual description of the receptor-specific causal interaction summarized from the analysis, such as receptor blockade reduced potentiation or receptor activation enhanced depression.

Citation or bibliographic reference supporting the summarized causal interaction, recorded as a string that can contain author-year, DOI, PMID, or journal reference. Example: Smith et al. 2021; PMID:12345678; doi:10.xxxx/xxxxx.
Type of evidence supporting the derived summary entry. Examples: original_experiment, replicated_finding, review_support, meta_analysis, not_specified.
Qualitative confidence assigned to the derived summary entry based on consistency of evidence supporting the causal interaction. Examples: high, medium, low, uncertain.
Number of source studies, analyses, or evidence records contributing to the summarized causal interaction row in the derived table.
Version label or release identifier for the derived causal plasticity summary table, recorded to track updates to the compiled evidence set. Example: v1.0, 2024_08_release.
